composers_checked.name: Röntgen, Julius
composers_checked.note: 3 IMSLP pages kept; 25 recorded works found by the gap check (16 string trios, Piano Trios 4/9/10, clarinet trio, 4 quartets, Piano Quintet in G). RECHECK 2026-10-17 added the Cobra (Parkanyi Quartet) quartets in C major and G minor ('Fancy') and Piano Quintet in G. Sextet in G major (1931; RCA 88697158372, Deezer 7060488, 21 min) still not entered: no source opened names its scoring. No full works list was found (en/nl Wikipedia lists gave 404), so only MusicBrainz (354 works, 290 recorded) and Deezer album searches back the gap check

note: Apple's search API stayed blocked (fetcher back-off) for most of the run, so recordings were found through MusicBrainz release data, label pages (Chandos, SOMM, Champs Hill), MusicWeb reviews and Concertzender listings; Naxos Music Library and Presto were not used. Composer names follow the input (IMSLP spelling: 'Lachner, Franz Paul', 'Rheinberger, Josef Gabriel'); the usual short forms would be 'Lachner, Franz' and 'Rheinberger, Josef'. RÖNTGEN is the big gap-check yield: 22 recorded works IMSLP lacks (Champs Hill/Naxos string trios Nos. 1-16, ARS piano trios, RCA clarinet trio, two quartets). Nos. 5-8 and 15 have no key because the sources disagree or omit it (No. 15 is 'C minor' on Champs Hill, 'C-sharp minor' on Naxos); years for Nos. 9-10 are inferred from 'the first of three trios from 1923' (No. 8); Nos. 11-12 have no year. His Sextet in G major (ARC Ensemble, RCA 88697158372) is left out because no source opened names its scoring (probably strings). Grieg's F-major quartet completed by Röntgen belongs to Grieg's slice. LACHNER: only Op. 75, 77 and 173 of the six quartets have a confirmed recording (Rodin Quartett, Amati; Concertzender broadcast listings, no catalogue numbers). The Rodin Quartett set seems to cover all six (a library record seen in a search lists 'String Quartets Vol. 3: Op. 75 & 77'), so Op. 76, 120 and 169 are probably recorded too; they are skipped until a listing is found, as are the two piano quintets (a forum post mentions a Thorofon recording of one, unconfirmed) and the Elegy for five cellos (IMSLP flags it 'recorded', nothing found). The Septet in E-flat (1824) comes from the gap check; its scoring (one violin, no bassoon) is from a concert review, while the Ensemble Villa Musica line-up on disc lists two violinists. BOTTESINI: the quartets on Dynamic DM8012 are numbered 1-3 (Op. 2-4) there but 'n. 2 op. 2' in Wikipedia's list, so they are titled by opus and BOT. number only; the B-flat and D-major IMSLP pages are matched to Op. 2 and Op. 4 by key. 'Duetto' and 'Capriccio Op. 19' are works for two solo instruments with piano accompaniment (three players) kept as trios. RHEINBERGER: the Suite Op. 149 is entered in its original trio form (organ, violin, cello; Hofmeister says the string-orchestra version followed in 1891); Op. 191 also exists as the composer's Sextet Op. 191b for piano and winds (no strings, out). PUCCINI: the 'String Quartet in D major' is a single surviving movement; the Scherzo in A minor (58 seconds) is entered because it is recorded; the three student fugues on Urania LDV14111 are not entered. RECHECK 2026-10-17: 7 works added (Lachner: String Quartets Op. 76, Op. 120, Op. 169 and Piano Quintet No. 2 Op. 145; Röntgen: String Quartets in C major and in G minor ("Fancy"), Piano Quintet in G major); 12 lines settled as not performed or recorded (Lachner 7, Rheinberger WoO 53, Bottesini 3; Bottesini's Passione amorosa moved to 'doubtful: low confidence'); 3 still partly unchecked (concert programmes for Lachner Op. 139, Op. 121 and Bottesini's Quartet No. 6, which have modern editions); hand edits: Lachner Opp. 75, 77 and 173 now cite the Rodin Quartett Amati albums (Deezer 593432432 Vol. 3 = Op. 75+77; 593456482 Vol. 1 = Op. 169+173; Vol. 2 593456412 = Op. 76+120) in floor.recorded and sources and go from medium to high; Apple lists the same three volumes. Op. 145 has no key in its title: IMSLP says A minor, de.wikipedia C minor (and swaps the keys of Op. 139/145 against Schott's 'C minor' for Op. 139). Op. 120 and 169 years are composition dates (IMSLP 1849 and 1875 print; de.wikipedia 1849 for both). Cobra Part 2 also holds wind and vocal works (out of scope). Not entered: Röntgen's Sextet in G (scoring unconfirmed); Bottesini's audite album 'Music for Double-Bass and String Quintet' (Bunya, Deezer 6031806), showpieces with quartet accompaniment by an unknown arranger.
